newsitem.title: INDIA: India proposes state-level power regulators.
newsitem.headline: India proposes state-level power regulators.

text.p: The Indian government, in a measure aimed to attract foreign investment, has proposed a plan to set up state-level regulators to fix power tariffs, a senior official said on Monday.

The federal government had worked on a "common minimum action plan" under which state governments would agree to set up regulatory commissions for the power industry, Power Secretary P. Abraham told a business conference.
"We have to place the proposals before the new government," Abraham, the top-ranking civil servant in the Power Ministry, told the conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).

Inder Kumar Gujral of the centre-left United Front was sworn in as India's new prime minister on Monday at the end of a three-week long political crisis following the withdrawal of critical support by the Congress party on March 30.

The United Front coalition formed a new government under Gujral, who replaced H.D. Deve Gowda as prime minister in order to meet a condition set by the Congress for resumption of its support. Deve Gowda lost a confidence vote on April 11.

India has been seeking billions of dollars in private and foreign investment to build power generation facilities, but prospective investors have been wary of state-level power distribution companies that would pay for the electricity.
The state utilities, many of them in poor financial condition, charge power tariffs described by investors as too low to be economically viable.
Abraham said at least 10 of India's 26 states had already started or were in the process of starting a process of privatisation in power distribution.
Power distribution is a matter under the jurisdiction of state governments under the Indian constitution.

Many state governments have been reluctant to restructure their poorly-performing electricity boards or hike power tariffs, fearing political problems in cutting down staff or in offending farmers who receive subsidised electricity.
